document.title: MOSIP Face Liveness & Presentation Attack Detection (PAD) Service — API Documentation
document.revision_note: Revision 3 documents the complete, verified REST API surface of the service across all 4 tiers (Client-Facing, Authenticated, Operator-Keyed, and Supervisor-Keyed), covering all 28 endpoints. It documents user session authentication (V12), supervisor policy gating, operator API key access, in-memory rate limiting (RateLimitFilter), security headers (SecurityHeadersFilter), tamper-evident audit chaining (V7-V9), anti-replay session nonces (V13), and client evidence verification.
document.generated_from: the source code and route inventory of this repository, cross-checked against RouteInventory.java and the running service
verification_method: Every endpoint, status code, error body and response field below was cross-checked against RouteInventory.java, ApiRouteInventoryTest.java, and controller unit/integration tests.
The endpoint inventory is aligned with RouteInventory.java (28 endpoints across 4 disjoint security tiers: 16 Client-Facing, 3 Authenticated, 3 Operator-Keyed, and 6 Supervisor-Keyed).

Behaviour not reachable without a real biometric face (PAD rejection, passive score clearing the threshold, active-challenge success) is derived from source reading and is marked derived_from_source where it appears.
document.verified_environment: JDK 17, dev profile (in-memory H2, Flyway disabled, ddl-auto create-drop); the JVM default offset observed in every response was +05:30
not_verified: The default profile (PostgreSQL + Flyway) was not exercised. The timestamp defect in known_issues was observed on H2 only and may behave differently on PostgreSQL.
ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE (503) was not reproduced — OpenCV loaded successfully in the verification environment. The handler exists and /health reports the engine state.
documentation_scope: Every HTTP endpoint exposed by this service (controllers in io.mosip.liveness.api) — 28 paths across 4 security tiers
Request and response payloads as serialized by Jackson (DTOs in io.mosip.liveness.dto)
Validation rules that are actually enforced, and their exact error text
Cross-cutting behaviour that exists: the error envelope, null-field omission, CORS as configured, and the size limits that are really in effect
Known defects and gaps, so integrators are not surprised at runtime
not_in_scope: The in-process client adapters (io.mosip.liveness.client.DesktopLivenessAdapter / AndroidLivenessAdapter) — they call this API in-process, they are not endpoints
The L0/L1 device abstraction layer (io.mosip.liveness.device) — a library interface, not HTTP

The standalone engine layer (io.mosip.liveness.engine.FaceLivenessEngine / LivenessDecisionLogic) and the eval harness (io.mosip.liveness.eval.AttackScenarioHarness). This layer implements median-window passive voting, challenge windows and repeated-failure actions, but the REST controllers do not use it: nothing in io.mosip.liveness.api or io.mosip.liveness.services references it. See known_issues.engine_layer_unused_by_http.
The legacy Python scaffold under pad_liveness_backend/ — superseded by this Java service
The model backends under io.mosip.liveness.backend — not invoked by the HTTP decision path
document.note: Fields whose value is null are omitted from responses (Jackson default-property-inclusion: non_null). Field names are camelCase. Timestamps are ISO-8601 but their offset is not stable — see conventions.timestamps.

port_configurable_via: SERVER_PORT environment variable (application.yml binds server.port to ${SERVER_PORT:8000})
server.launcher: scripts/start.sh (and scripts/start.bat). It builds if needed, waits for /health, then opens the console. There is no start script at the repository root.
server.browser_test_console: http://localhost:8000/ (the bundled static console; browsers only expose the camera on a secure origin, so open it on localhost)

profiles.dev: in-memory H2, Flyway disabled, ddl-auto create-drop — used by scripts/start.sh
profiles.default: PostgreSQL with Flyway migrations, ddl-auto validate

conventions.null_handling: null fields are omitted from JSON responses

observed_forms: Freshly created or freshly updated objects serialized from memory: the JVM default offset, e.g. 2026-10-10T23:05:36.1755725+05:30 (7 fractional digits)
Objects read back from the database: UTC with a Z suffix and microsecond precision, e.g. 2026-10-10T12:06:20.834717Z
timestamps.warning: On the H2 dev profile the two forms are not the same instant for the same row, and repeated read-back shifts the value further. Do not do timestamp arithmetic across responses. See known_issues.timestamps_and_duration_shift.

conventions.enums: serialized by name in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, except config/DB challenge types which use lower snake case (see enumerations.ChallengeType_wire_values)
conventions.frame_encoding: base64-encoded JPEG (or PNG) bytes. A data-URI prefix (data:image/jpeg;base64,...) is tolerated and stripped; plain base64 is the expected form.
conventions.idempotency: frame submission is not idempotent: every accepted frame is scored and recorded again. Re-submitting the same bytes produces an identical-looking response but a new FrameEvent row, and it consumes the session's frame rate budget in any deployment that adds one.

authentication.summary: Multi-tier security model enforcing role-based access control, operator API keys, session tokens, and fail-closed supervisor authorization.

tiers.description: Reachable without authentication. Drives session creation, frame ingestion, challenge validation, evidence verification, public policy reads, and health/metrics.
Reachable by any valid user session (MOSIP_SESSION HttpOnly cookie or Authorization: Bearer). Allows inspecting own user info, logging out, and changing password.

Reachable by callers presenting a valid X-Operator-API-Key matching MOSIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY (or an authenticated session with OPERATOR/SUPERVISOR role). Grants read access to role probe, operator session feeds, and rejections.

Reachable strictly by authenticated sessions holding the SUPERVISOR role. Protects configuration updates (PUT /config/{workflowType}), threshold sweeps (/eval/threshold-sweep), and user administration (/users/**).

cookie_auth.storage: SHA-256 hash stored in DB (V12__auth_users_and_tokens.sql); plaintext token never stored

operator_key.configuration: MOSIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY (min 16 chars; blank means all operator-keyed routes refuse requests)

anti_replay.session_nonce: 256-bit cryptographically secure random nonce generated upon session creation (V13__session_anti_replay.sql)
anti_replay.evidence_verification: POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/evidence validates session nonce, time window, and cryptographic signature before accepting client-signed liveness evidence

audit_chain.hashing: HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with MOSIP_AUDIT_HMAC_SECRET (falls back to SHA-256 if unset)
audit_chain.chain_structure: prev_hash -> entry_hash chaining on CONFIG_CHANGED events in audit_logs
audit_chain.database_protection: PostgreSQL triggers reject UPDATE and DELETE operations on audit_logs

authorization_notes: Individual user accounts hold either OPERATOR or SUPERVISOR role.
Policy updates require SUPERVISOR authentication and automatically audit the old -> new values and risk classification in the tamper-evident audit chain.
A session is the unit of consent for one liveness check, bound to a unique cryptographic nonce.

rate_limiting.detail: RateLimitFilter provides in-memory token bucket rate limiting across four distinct request categories with budget headers returned on all requests.

buckets.name: operator-key
buckets.applies_to: Operator key probe and feed reads

enforced_by_bean_validation.SessionCreateRequest.workflowType: @NotNull -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR 'workflowType: workflow_type is required' when absent; an unknown name such as 'FOO' is a deserialization failure and returns 'Request body is malformed or unreadable.' instead
enforced_by_bean_validation.SessionCreateRequest.deviceId: @NotBlank -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR 'deviceId: device_id is required' when absent or blank
enforced_by_bean_validation.ChallengeValidateRequest.framesBase64: @NotEmpty -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR 'framesBase64: frames_base64 must contain at least one frame'; no maximum
enforced_by_bean_validation.ConfigPolicyUpdate.passiveThreshold: @Min(0) @Max(1) -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR outside [0,1]. 0 and 1 are accepted, so a threshold of 0 makes every frame that reaches scoring pass
enforced_by_bean_validation.ConfigPolicyUpdate.challengeTimeoutMs: @Min(1000) @Max(60000) — there is no higher floor than 1000 ms
enforced_by_bean_validation.ConfigPolicyUpdate.challengeTypes: not annotated; an empty list is rejected in the controller with 400 BAD_REQUEST
enforced_by_bean_validation.note: Bean-validation failures are reported one field per response as '<field>: <message>'; several fields failing at once are joined with '; '.

response_body.message: Request body exceeds the configured limit.

decoded_frame.downscale: none — frames are decoded at their native size and analysed as-is (there is no resize on the request path)
decoded_frame.supported_input: anything OpenCV's imdecode can read (JPEG, PNG, ...); failures return 422 INVALID_FRAME with 'Frame could not be decoded as an image'

active_challenge_burst.note: validateActive requires at least 2 frames to evaluate any action; a 1-frame burst is accepted (200) but can never pass a challenge.
active_challenge_burst.earlier_revision_claim: Revision 1 documented a maximum of 60 frames. Not enforced.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

security_headers.csp_exemptions: Paths starting with /swagger-ui, /v3/api-docs, or /webjars omit CSP to allow bundled UI webjar scripts, while retaining all other security headers.

cors.detail: Local development ports are matched via allowedOriginPatterns(...). Credentials stay false as the HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie is scoped to the host origin, while cross-origin callers use Authorization: Bearer.

shape.status: HTTP status code as a number

error_handling.revision_3_status: All standard HTTP error codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 422, 429, 500, 503) are fully active and tested across filters and handlers.

WorkflowType.applies_to: session creation, config endpoints, session responses
WorkflowType.notes: Distinct from the engine-level enum (RESIDENT_REGISTRATION, OPERATOR_AUTH, SUPERVISOR_AUTH); ConfigService owns the mapping.

SessionStatus.notes: EXPIRED is set when an ACTIVE session is closed explicitly via POST .../close.

ChallengeStatus.notes: TIMEOUT is declared but is never written by the HTTP path: no challenge window is evaluated. Only the standalone engine layer sets it.

ChallengeType_wire_values.notes: Two spellings exist on the wire. Config and DB rows use lower snake case; challenge responses and frame responses use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE names.
ChallengeType_wire_values.mapping_note: The wire name TURN_LEFT corresponds to the engine challenge TURN_HEAD_LEFT (and TURN_RIGHT to TURN_HEAD_RIGHT), which is how it appears in EffectivePolicy.allowedChallenges. Config values that are not recognised map to BLINK rather than failing: the conversion falls back to ChallengeType.BLINK for any unknown name.
ChallengeType_wire_values.persistence_note: Challenge rows store the name in upper snake case (for example TURN_LEFT), while the config row stores the lower-case form.

PadAttackType.notes: OTHER is a valid value. In the current heuristic PAD implementation the SCREEN_REPLAY branch cannot be reached (see known_issues.pad_heuristic_limits).

FrameAction.notes: The action vocabulary the frame endpoint actually returns.

values.proceed: liveness satisfied — session PASSED (passive score at or above the threshold)
values.escalate_to_active: a challenge is required; the payload carries it
values.retry_passive: non-terminal: either no face was observed or more than one face was observed. Keep submitting frames.
values.reject: terminal failure: confirmed presentation attack, or passive score below the threshold with active liveness disabled

ChallengeAction.notes: The action vocabulary the challenge validation endpoint actually returns.

values.retry_challenge: a NEW challenge is returned in the payload. Emitted both when the submitted challenge passed but minChallengeCount is not yet satisfied, and when the attempt failed with retry budget remaining
values.reject: terminal failure: PAD attack detected in the burst, or the retry budget is exhausted

ChallengeAction.not_present: There is no 'continue' action and no challenge time window. The first validation that does not detect the requested action fails the challenge and increments retryCount.

workflowType.notes: @NotNull. An unknown value is rejected as unreadable JSON: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR 'Request body is malformed or unreadable.'

deviceId.notes: @NotBlank; blank and whitespace-only values are rejected. Your label for the L0/L1 device.

subjectRef.notes: optional opaque reference from the client (for example an applicant id). It is stored but not echoed back — SessionResponse has no subjectRef field.

online.notes: client-declared connectivity; recorded with the session and echoed back. It does not change enforcement.

finalResult.notes: omitted while the session is undecided

SessionResponse.no_policy_field: There is no policy field and no policy snapshot. The workflow policy is re-read from the database on every frame, so a config edit does take effect on an in-flight session — the opposite of an immutable snapshot.

finalResult.notes: omitted for a session closed while ACTIVE, because it was never decided

totalFramesEvaluated.notes: count of recorded frame events, including frames with no face

durationMs.notes: elapsed time between createdAt and closedAt. Unreliable in this build — see known_issues.timestamps_and_duration_shift.

frameBase64.notes: @NotBlank only. base64 image bytes; no data-URI prefix required.

stage.notes: the stage of the session when the frame was processed

faceQuality.notes: 0..1 OpenCV heuristic computed over the WHOLE frame (0.5 x Laplacian sharpness + 0.5 x brightness proximity to mid-grey); present only when a single face was observed. The configured minFaceQuality (0.50) is NOT enforced anywhere on this path — it is reported, not used as a gate.

livenessScore.notes: 0..1 passive score for THIS frame only: 0.4 x faceQuality + 0.4 x eyeSymmetry + 0.2 x sharpness, where eyeSymmetry is 1.0 when the eye cascade finds two or more eyes in the face box and 0.4 otherwise. There is no sliding window and no median: the single value is compared with the threshold. Present only on frames that were scored (a frame with no face omits it).

padFlag.notes: true when this frame's PAD verdict flagged an attack

timeoutMs.notes: copied from the configured challengeTimeoutMs (8000 by default). It is informational: no timer is enforced.

attemptNumber.notes: 1 for the challenge issued on escalation

message.notes: safe, user-facing text intended to be shown to the subject

FrameProcessResult.field_that_does_not_exist: mayRetrySession. Revision 1 described it as declared-but-never-populated; it is not declared at all. Clients must read the session status and failureReason instead.

no_face.message: No face detected. Please position your face in the frame.

multiple_faces.message: Multiple faces detected. Only one person may be captured at a time.

pad_rejected.message: Face verification could not be completed. Please try again.
pad_rejected.note: Only reached when the workflow has no challenge stage to hand the verdict to. With an active stage, a confirmed hit answers escalate_to_active instead.

pad_escalated.note: A confirmed hit is carried by the escalation, so the client can name the attack behind the challenge instead of showing a clean frame.

passive_failed_active_disabled.message: We could not verify face liveness. Please try again.

challengeId.notes: @NotNull (not @NotBlank, which would throw on a UUID)

framesBase64.notes: the frame burst captured while the subject performed the action. At least 2 frames are needed for any action to be detectable.

challenge.notes: the challenge that now matters for the client: on retry_challenge this is the NEWLY issued challenge (the submitted one is already PASSED or FAILED)

padFlag.notes: set (true) only when this check ended as a presentation attack; the challenge's frames are re-run through both PAD sources, so a replay cannot clear a passive-stage flag by performing the action

presentation_attack.message: Face verification could not be completed. Please try again.

second_challenge.message: Action detected. One more check required.

attempt_failed_budget_remains.message: We could not verify that action. Let's try a different one.
attempt_failed_budget_remains.note: retryCount is incremented on the first undetected burst — there is no 'still within the window' state.

retries_exhausted.message: We could not verify face liveness. Please try again.

attemptNumber.notes: counts the challenges issued for the session: the challenge created on escalation is 1, and each replacement increments. It is not a count of failed attempts

completedAt.notes: omitted while the challenge is still ISSUED

ConfigPolicyUpdate.notes: Partial update: omit any field to leave it unchanged. There is no cross-field or merged-policy validation: each field is checked on its own, so combinations that are internally inconsistent (for example minChallengeCount larger than the configured challenge pool) are accepted.

livenessEnabled.notes: stored and returned, but NOT consulted by the decision path: setting it to false does not skip scoring or challenges in this build

passiveThreshold.notes: @Min(0) @Max(1). 0 is accepted even though it makes every scored frame pass (only frames that reach scoring — a missing face still cannot pass)

activeLivenessEnabled.notes: this one IS honoured: false turns a below-threshold passive score into an immediate terminal failure instead of a challenge

minChallengeCount.notes: not checked against the size of challengeTypes

challengeTypes.notes: lower snake case. An empty array is refused with 400 BAD_REQUEST; unknown names silently fall back to BLINK

challengeTimeoutMs.notes: stored, echoed in challenge payloads, and never enforced

maxRetryCount.notes: the session fails when retryCount >= maxRetryCount, evaluated after the increment, so with the default 3 a session survives 2 failed bursts and fails on the 3rd

onRepeatedFailure.notes: stored and returned, but NOT applied by the HTTP path: retry exhaustion always returns action 'reject' with failureReason 'max_retries_exceeded' regardless of this setting

ConfigPolicyResponse.defaults: A row is created on first access using ONE hard-coded default set for every workflow: passiveThreshold 0.75, activeLivenessEnabled true, minChallengeCount 1, challengeTypes [blink, smile, turn_left, turn_right], challengeTimeoutMs 8000, maxRetryCount 3, onRepeatedFailure LOCK. Verified for RESIDENT, OPERATOR and SUPERVISOR alike — the three workflows are not differentiated in this build. (V1__init_schema.sql seeds the same values into all three rows.)

returned_by: POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/frames and .../challenges/validate (in-process only: decision-time re-read, not returned to the client)
EffectivePolicy.notes: The fully-resolved policy the decision path uses: the stored DB row merged with hard-coded engine defaults. Values that have no DB column (minFaceQuality, passiveMinFrames, passiveWindowFrames, maxSessionDurationMs, frameSamplingRate, frameSamplingMinFps, combined weights) are constants, not configuration.

minFaceQuality.notes: constant 0.5; not enforced as a gate

passiveMinFrames.notes: constant 5; not used — there is no cold-start window

passiveWindowFrames.notes: constant 7; not used — there is no median window

allowedChallenges.notes: engine challenge names (BLINK, SMILE, TURN_HEAD_LEFT, TURN_HEAD_RIGHT, LOOK_DIRECTION, ...), derived from the DB challengeTypes. An empty or fully unrecognised list falls back to BLINK rather than failing

onRepeatedFailure.notes: engine naming of the DB value; not applied by the HTTP path

passiveThresholdActive.notes: reported as the same value as passiveThreshold; the active stage does not re-score passives separately

maxSessionDurationMs.notes: constant 30000; not enforced — sessions do not expire on their own

frameSamplingRate.notes: constant 2; no sampling is performed by the API

frameSamplingMinFps.notes: constant 15; not enforced — there is no frame-rate gate

combinedPassiveWeight.notes: constant 0.4; no combined score is computed

combinedActiveWeight.notes: constant 0.6; no combined score is computed

eventType.notes: the HTTP path writes exactly five values: PAD_REJECTED, SESSION_PASSED, CHALLENGE_ISSUED, CHALLENGE_PASSED, CHALLENGE_FAILED

details.notes: event-specific payload, always present (an empty object when the event carries nothing). PAD_REJECTED carries attackType, confidence and stage; SESSION_PASSED carries via; CHALLENGE_* carry challengeType; CHALLENGE_ISSUED also carries attemptNumber and timeoutMs

AuditLogEntry.no_workflow_type_field: There is no workflowType field in this payload.
AuditLogEntry.sparsity: The trail is intentionally sparse on the request path: a frame that is rejected for having no face or multiple faces writes a FrameEvent row but NO audit row, so a session that only ever saw unusable frames returns an empty array (verified: [] after two no-face frames). There is also no SESSION_CREATED, FRAME_SCORED, MAX_RETRIES_EXCEEDED or CONFIG_CHANGED entry, and no per-session config-change record of any kind.

passRate.notes: passedSessions / totalSessions, rounded to 4 decimals; 0.0 when there are no sessions

avgPassiveToActiveEscalationRate.notes: distinct sessions that recorded at least one frame in the ACTIVE stage, divided by totalSessions

livenessRetryRate.notes: sum of session retryCount divided by totalSessions

padRejectionRate.notes: sessions whose failureReason starts with 'presentation_attack:' divided by totalSessions

OperationalMetrics.notes: These eleven fields are the complete response. There is no pipeline-timing block (no decode/facedetect/onnxscore phases are measured) and no rate-limit counters. All values are derived from the database on each call; nothing here is in-memory-only.

endpoints.summary: Liveness of the service and of the frame-processing engine
endpoints.description: Reports whether the process is up and whether the OpenCV native library loaded. Frame-processing endpoints cannot work when the engine is unavailable.

response.notes: engine is 'available' or 'unavailable'; the value reflects native-library loading at startup, not a per-request probe.

use_cases: Startup readiness probe (scripts/start.sh waits on this)
Container or orchestrator health check
Diagnose a frame endpoint returning 503

endpoints.summary: Start a liveness/PAD session
endpoints.description: Stores the session with status ACTIVE, stage PASSIVE and retryCount 0. No policy snapshot is taken and no cross-field policy validation happens here: the workflow policy is looked up from the database on every frame and on every challenge validation.

201.notes: online defaults to true when omitted

400.when: workflowType missing or unknown, deviceId missing or blank, or the body is empty/unreadable

use_cases: Resident face capture during enrolment
Operator biometric authentication
Supervisor biometric authentication

endpoints.summary: Read the current state of a session
endpoints.description: Returns the session row as stored. There is no policy snapshot on it, so this call does not tell you which operating point the session was created under — read GET /api/v1/config/{workflowType}/effective instead, bearing in mind that a config edit changes the effective policy for sessions that are already in flight.

500.when: sessionId is not a valid UUID — the type conversion failure is not handled and falls through to the catch-all handler (verified)

use_cases: Poll the final state after a terminal frame response, once the session has stopped accepting frames
Confirm the retry budget a session consumed

endpoints.summary: Submit one face frame for passive liveness + PAD + policy decision
endpoints.description: The core decision endpoint. Per frame it: re-reads the workflow policy from the database; detects faces with a Haar cascade and treats multiple faces as retryable; runs the PAD heuristics and rejects on the first flagged frame; then, for a single detected face, computes a per-frame passive score and compares it directly with passiveThreshold. At or above the threshold the session PASSES; below it the session escalates to an active challenge (a challenge is selected from allowedChallenges and persisted), or fails immediately when active liveness is disabled for the workflow. There is no sliding window, no median vote and no cold-start stage: the first usable frame can pass or fail the session. The decision path never consults livenessEnabled.

200.notes: action decides what the client does next. A 200 does not mean the frame was usable.

400.when: frameBase64 missing or blank; malformed JSON

409.when: session is not ACTIVE; message pattern 'Session is not active (status=...)'

422.when: the payload is not decodable base64, or not an image OpenCV can read

503.when: the OpenCV native library is unavailable

action_meanings.retry_passive: non-terminal — keep streaming frames (no face, multiple faces, or a presentation attack was flagged)
action_meanings.escalate_to_active: present challenge.challengeType to the subject, collect a burst, then call challenge validate
action_meanings.reject: terminal — session FAILED (confirmed presentation attack, or passive score below the threshold with active liveness disabled)

verified_no_face.message: No face detected. Please position your face in the frame.

verified_invalid_frame.message: Frame could not be decoded as an image

use_cases: Streaming L0/L1 face frames during resident capture
Demonstrating that a PAD-flagged frame is terminal and never earns a challenge
Building a client loop: keep submitting while action is retry_passive, switch flow on escalate_to_active, and stop on proceed or reject

endpoints.summary: Submit the frame burst captured during an active challenge
endpoints.description: Re-runs PAD over the burst first (an attack here is terminal). The requested action is then evaluated across the burst (at least 2 frames are required). If it was observed, the challenge PASSES: when the number of PASSED challenges for the session has reached minChallengeCount the session PASSES, otherwise a NEW challenge is issued and returned with action retry_challenge. If the action was NOT observed, the challenge FAILS immediately, retryCount is incremented, and the response is retry_challenge with a new challenge while budget remains, or reject once retryCount >= maxRetryCount. no challenge window is evaluated and no TIMEOUT status is produced.

400.when: challengeId missing; framesBase64 missing or empty

404.when: the session does not exist, or the challenge does not exist or belongs to a different session ('Challenge not found for this session')

409.when: the session is not ACTIVE, or the challenge is not ISSUED (already PASSED, FAILED or TIMEOUT)

422.when: a frame in the burst is not decodable

action_meanings.retry_challenge: use the newly returned challenge.challengeId for the next validation — the submitted one is closed
action_meanings.reject: terminal; session FAILED (PAD attack in the burst, or the retry budget is exhausted)

endpoints.client_rule: Always drive the NEXT validation from the challenge object in the response, never from the one you submitted: after retry_challenge the submitted challenge is already resolved and reusing it returns 409.

verified_empty_burst.message: framesBase64: frames_base64 must contain at least one frame

verified_unknown_challenge.message: Challenge not found for this session

use_cases: Active liveness (blink, smile, head turn) after a passive score below the threshold
A workflow that demands more than one challenge before acceptance (raise minChallengeCount)

endpoints.summary: Close a session explicitly and return an audit-friendly summary
endpoints.description: If the session is still ACTIVE it is marked EXPIRED and closedAt is set; if it is already terminal its outcome is preserved and the same summary is returned again (the call is safe to repeat). The summary aggregates frames evaluated, challenges issued, retries and duration.

examples.note_on_durationMs: The value above belongs to a session that lived about 5 seconds; it is inflated by the JVM UTC offset (5 h 30 min plus the real 5.4 s). See known_issues.timestamps_and_duration_shift.

use_cases: Abandoned capture (subject walked away), so the session does not linger ACTIVE
End-of-flow summary for the operator UI

endpoints.summary: Audit trail for one session, oldest first
endpoints.description: Every audit row recorded for the session, in chronological order. Rows exist only for the events the request path actually logs: PAD_REJECTED, SESSION_PASSED, CHALLENGE_ISSUED, CHALLENGE_PASSED, CHALLENGE_FAILED. Frames that were unusable (no face, multiple faces) produce a FrameEvent but no audit row, so this can legitimately be empty for a session that submitted frames. Unknown session ids also return an empty array rather than 404.

200.notes: [] when the session has no logged events — including when the session does not exist

use_cases: Explain a failure to an operator without exposing model internals to the subject
Evidence for an auditor of what was checked and what the verdict was — noting the sparse coverage listed in AuditLogEntry.sparsity

endpoints.summary: Read the stored policy row for a workflow
endpoints.description: Returns the policy as stored in config_policies. If no row exists it is created on the spot from a single hard-coded default set, so reading RESIDENT, OPERATOR and SUPERVISOR yields identical values in this build.

500.when: the workflow name is not one of the three — the enum conversion failure is unhandled (verified with /api/v1/config/FOO). A 400 would be correct here.

use_cases: Operator UI showing the current thresholds before changing them
Confirming which fields are editable at runtime

endpoints.summary: Read the computed policy exactly as the decision path sees it
endpoints.description: The stored config merged with hard-coded engine defaults — the real operating point, including fields that are not editable through the API (face-quality value, frame counts, active-stage threshold, session duration, sampling rates, combined weights). Use this, not the session response, to know what a session is being held to.

500.when: the workflow name is not one of the three

use_cases: Diagnose why a session behaves differently from the API's editable fields
Confirm a policy edit took effect without opening a session

endpoints.summary: Update a workflow's policy at runtime
endpoints.description: Partial update with no redeploy: omitted fields keep their stored value, and the decision path re-reads the row on the next frame, so an edit changes sessions that are already in flight. Validation is per field only. The change is written to config_policies; it is NOT recorded anywhere else — there is no change history, no diff, no actor and no risk classification.
endpoints.auth: NONE — this endpoint is open. Nothing is validated in front of the body.

200.notes: the full stored policy after the merge

examples: minChallengeCount: must be greater than or equal to 1 (VALIDATION_ERROR)
passiveThreshold: must be less than or equal to 1 (VALIDATION_ERROR)
challengeTimeoutMs: must be greater than or equal to 1000 (VALIDATION_ERROR)
maxRetryCount: must be less than or equal to 10 (VALIDATION_ERROR)
onRepeatedFailure must be one of: LOCK, ESCALATE, ALLOW_RETRY (BAD_REQUEST)
challengeTypes must not be empty when activeLiveness is enabled (BAD_REQUEST)

500.when: the workflow name is not one of the three

endpoints.effect_timing: Applies to the next frame of every session of that workflow, including sessions created earlier.

verified_rejected_combination.note: Accepted even though five challenges cannot be drawn from a one-type pool. Revision 1 claimed this combination was refused.

endpoints.summary: Anonymized operational metrics
endpoints.description: Session-level counts and rates computed from the database. No PII and no per-session attribution.
use_cases: Measure pass, escalation, retry and PAD-rejection rates before tuning a threshold
Feed a review with aggregate numbers rather than session records

endpoints.summary: Start manual active-liveness challenge on demand
endpoints.description: Issues a manual challenge for an active or passed session. Validated as an extra check that records to audit logs without rewriting an already PASSED verdict.

409.when: session status is invalid or active liveness disabled

endpoints.summary: Check client liveness evidence against its session
endpoints.description: Checks a client-produced liveness evidence payload against the session the server holds. Rejects when the session is not ACTIVE/PASSED, the nonce does not match the session nonce (V13), completedEpochMs precedes startedEpochMs, or any challengeResults entry is false. Warns (still verified) on a bypassed gate, a completion timestamp well before session creation, or a missing signatureHex: presence of a signature is checked, not its cryptographic validity.

400.when: invalid payload, or a missing/blank sessionId or nonceHex

endpoints.summary: Change history for configuration policies
endpoints.description: Returns chronological audit trail of CONFIG_CHANGED events showing actor, before/after values, diff, and computed risk classification.

endpoints.summary: Cryptographically verify config audit chain integrity
endpoints.description: Traverses the prev_hash -> entry_hash chain of CONFIG_CHANGED audit records, verifying HMAC-SHA-256 signatures and reporting any gaps, tampering, or content mutations.

endpoints.summary: Local real-time diagnostic performance metrics
endpoints.description: Returns recent frame pipeline timings, FPS, score distributions, and backend info. Opt-in via mosip.liveness.diagnostics-enabled; restricted to loopback callers (answers 404 otherwise).

404.description: Returned when diagnostics are disabled or caller is non-loopback

endpoints.summary: Authenticate user credentials and issue session
endpoints.description: Verifies username and password using BCrypt. Sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax MOSIP_SESSION cookie upon success. Metered to mitigate brute-force attempts.

endpoints.summary: Current authenticated user profile
endpoints.description: Returns user account details for the session token in the cookie or Authorization: Bearer header. Re-verifies account status from DB.

endpoints.summary: Change current user's password
endpoints.description: Validates current password and updates to new password. Revokes previous sessions, clears mustChangePassword flag, and issues a fresh session cookie.

endpoints.summary: Sign out and invalidate session
endpoints.description: Revokes current session token in database and clears the MOSIP_SESSION cookie. Idempotent.

204.description: No Content; Set-Cookie cleared with Max-Age=0

endpoints.summary: Probe caller role
endpoints.description: Returns caller's effective role (SUPERVISOR or OPERATOR) based on session token or X-Operator-API-Key.

endpoints.summary: Operator session feed
endpoints.description: Returns chronological list of recent sessions. Supports filtering by workflowType and status, and paginating up to 200 items.
endpoints.auth: X-Operator-API-Key or session token (OPERATOR or SUPERVISOR role)

endpoints.summary: Operator rejection and failure feed
endpoints.description: Aggregates failed sessions and PAD_REJECTED / CHALLENGE_FAILED audit events for triage.
endpoints.auth: X-Operator-API-Key or session token (OPERATOR or SUPERVISOR role)

endpoints.summary: Run threshold calibration sweep
endpoints.description: Sweeps passive thresholds over bona-fide and attack score distributions to calculate BPCER, APCER, and ACER curves, recommending optimal operating points.

endpoints.summary: List all user accounts
endpoints.description: Returns list of registered users and their roles/statuses. Password hashes and tokens are never returned.

endpoints.summary: Create user account
endpoints.description: Creates an operator or supervisor account with an initial temporary password. The account starts with mustChangePassword=true.

endpoints.summary: Update user account role, status, or password
endpoints.description: Updates account attributes. Password resets revoke all active user sessions. Protected by last-supervisor safeguard (cannot disable/demote last supervisor).

409.when: Attempting to disable or demote the last remaining supervisor

endpoints.summary: Delete user account
endpoints.description: Deletes user account and associated auth tokens. Protected by last-supervisor safeguard (refused with 409 if deleting the last active supervisor).

409.when: Attempting to delete the last remaining supervisor

use_cases.title: Resident enrolment — honest subject, no action required
steps: POST /api/v1/sessions {workflowType: RESIDENT, deviceId: L1-CAM-01} -> 201, status ACTIVE, stage PASSIVE
POST .../frames repeatedly with face frames -> retry_passive while no usable single face is present
The first frame whose face passes detection and whose score reaches passiveThreshold returns action: proceed, message: 'Liveness verified.', and the session becomes PASSED
GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/audit shows SESSION_PASSED with details.via = passive
use_cases.why_it_matters: Passive-first means the common case needs no subject action. Note that there is no cold-start phase: with a clean, sharp, two-eye frame the very first submission can pass.
use_cases.caveat: The passive score is an OpenCV heuristic (quality, eye count, sharpness), not a trained model, so it is sensitive to lighting and framing.

use_cases.title: Presentation attack — fail-closed rejection
steps: Subject presents a printed photo or a screen replay
POST .../frames -> the heuristics may flag the frame (padFlag true, padAttackType PRINTED_PHOTO or VIDEO_REPLAY)

A flagged frame is terminal immediately: action reject, message 'Face verification could not be completed. Please try again.', session FAILED with failureReason presentation_attack:<TYPE>, and an audit row PAD_REJECTED with the attack type and confidence
No challenge is ever issued for an attack
use_cases.why_it_matters: A rejected frame never earns a challenge, so an attack cannot buy extra attempts by design.
use_cases.caveat: The PAD heuristics are a placeholder: 60% of the verdict comes from comparing Laplacian texture variance against a fixed constant, so both false accepts and false rejects are expected. See known_issues.pad_heuristic_limits.

use_cases.title: Low passive score — active challenge
steps: Passive score below passiveThreshold (and activeLivenessEnabled true) -> action escalate_to_active with challenge {challengeId, challengeType, timeoutMs, attemptNumber} and a message such as 'Please blink.'
Client prompts the subject, collects at least 2 frames, then POST .../challenges/validate with the burst
The action must be present in the burst: the same challenge id cannot be submitted again — a resolved challenge returns 409
Observed -> action proceed (when the PASSED-challenge count reaches minChallengeCount) or retry_challenge with a NEW challenge
Not observed -> the challenge FAILS, retryCount increments, and the response is retry_challenge with a new challenge, or reject when the budget is exhausted
use_cases.why_it_matters: The retry budget is a session-level count of failed challenge attempts, and a fresh challenge is always returned with a fresh challengeId.
use_cases.caveat: There is no grace window: the first burst that misses the action costs a retry, so a client must not submit a burst until the subject has actually attempted the action. Burst length matters too — a one-frame burst can never satisfy any action type.

use_cases.title: Retries exhausted
steps: Each challenge validation that fails to detect the requested action increments retryCount
When retryCount reaches maxRetryCount (3 by default) the session becomes FAILED with failureReason 'max_retries_exceeded'
The final response is action reject with 'We could not verify face liveness. Please try again.'
The audit trail contains CHALLENGE_FAILED rows for the attempts; there is no MAX_RETRIES_EXCEEDED row
use_cases.why_it_matters: The budget is per session, so a new session is the only way to earn more attempts.
use_cases.caveat: onRepeatedFailure (LOCK/ESCALATE/ALLOW_RETRY) is stored and returned by the config API but is not applied here — every exhausted session ends as a plain rejection with no lock, escalation or fallback action, and no mayRetrySession flag exists to distinguish them.

use_cases.title: Tuning a policy without a redeploy
steps: GET /api/v1/metrics -> passRate, escalation rate, retry rate, PAD-rejection rate
PUT /api/v1/config/RESIDENT {passiveThreshold: <new value>} -> 200 with the stored policy (requires SUPERVISOR session)
GET /api/v1/config/RESIDENT/effective -> confirm the operating point the decision path will use
GET /api/v1/config/audit -> confirm the CONFIG_CHANGED event recorded the actor, diff, and risk rating in the HMAC audit chain
use_cases.why_it_matters: Runtime tunability is real and immediate.
use_cases.caveat: Config edits require SUPERVISOR authentication and are cryptographically recorded in the HMAC-SHA-256 audit chain with automated risk classification.

use_cases.title: Offline registration environment
steps: Run the service as a local process beside the Registration Client (same host or embedded)
All liveness, PAD, challenge issuance and action validation runs locally — no WAN dependency
Send online: false in session creation to record the client's connectivity state; enforcement is identical
Only policy or model updates need connectivity, through a separate channel
use_cases.why_it_matters: Network availability does not decide whether liveness security is enforced.

use_cases.title: Integrating an L0/L1 device
steps: Keep device SDK integration upstream (Common Face Capture Device Interface or device adapter pattern)
Decode device frames to JPEG/PNG bytes and base64-encode them (a data-URI prefix is tolerated)
Call POST /api/v1/sessions then POST .../frames per frame; use the device id as deviceId
Keep frames modest in size: there is no configured cap, but string values above about 20 million characters fail to parse (400). A 1280px long edge is a sensible working size.
Throttle client-side: the service does not rate limit
use_cases.why_it_matters: The service consumes decoded frames, so it stays independent of any specific vendor.

known_issues.status: RESOLVED: PUT /api/v1/config/{workflowType} is protected by SupervisorGateFilter (requires SUPERVISOR role). Edits are recorded in HMAC-SHA-256 chained audit logs with risk classifications.
known_issues.detail: Historical issue: PUT /api/v1/config/{workflowType} previously had no authentication.
known_issues.resolution: Enforced by SupervisorGateFilter (401/403) and audited to audit_logs via ConfigController.auditPolicyChange.

known_issues.status: RESOLVED: AppConfig uses allowedOriginPatterns('http://localhost:*', 'http://127.0.0.1:*') to support wildcard ports for local development tools.
known_issues.detail: Historical issue: AppConfig previously used allowedOrigins with wildcard ports, which failed literal match.
known_issues.resolution: Switched to allowedOriginPatterns and exposed rate limiting headers.

known_issues.detail: On the H2 dev profile a timestamp written as local time comes back from the database as UTC, and each further read-back shifts it again. SessionSummary.durationMs is computed from a database-read createdAt and an in-memory closedAt, so it inherits the offset error and reports roughly 5 h 30 min more than the real elapsed time on a host at UTC+05:30.
known_issues.verified: A session created at local 23:06:20.834717+05:30 read back immediately as 2026-10-10T12:06:20.834717Z, and after closing as 2026-10-10T06:36:20.834717Z. Closing that ~3-second-old session reported durationMs 19803230 (5.5 hours plus 3 seconds).
known_issues.recommended_fix: Pin the JDBC timezone (for example spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.jdbc.time_zone=UTC), store instants consistently, and compute durationMs from a single consistent source. Verify against the PostgreSQL profile as well — this was observed on H2 only.

known_issues.status: RESOLVED: GlobalExceptionHandler includes dedicated MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException (400 VALIDATION_ERROR) and NoResourceFoundException (404 NOT_FOUND). GET /api/v1/config/audit is explicitly routed.
known_issues.detail: Historical issue: Unhandled type conversions and route collisions fell through to 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.
known_issues.resolution: Dedicated exception handlers return structured 400/404 envelopes with user-safe error messages.

known_issues.detail: PadEngineService is a placeholder. The screen-replay branch compares a hard-coded freqRatio = 0.1 against a 0.35 threshold, so SCREEN_REPLAY can never be returned. The remaining signals are Laplacian texture variance (< 15 -> PRINTED_PHOTO) and brightness (< 0.15 -> VIDEO_REPLAY). The ONNX/TFLite backends in io.mosip.liveness.backend are not used by the HTTP path.
known_issues.verified: Source reading; SCREEN_REPLAY unreachable by construction.
known_issues.recommended_fix: Implement real frequency analysis or wire a trained model into the decision path before making accuracy claims.

known_issues.detail: livenessEnabled is stored, returned and never read by the decision path: setting it to false does not skip scoring or challenges, and no LIVENESS_DISABLED audit event is written (the string does not exist in the codebase).
known_issues.verified: grep for livenessEnabled over services/ and api/ finds only ConfigController copying it into responses.
known_issues.recommended_fix: Either honour the flag with an audit record, or remove it from the public contract.

known_issues.detail: challengeTimeoutMs, maxSessionDurationMs, frameSamplingRate, frameSamplingMinFps, passiveThresholdActive, combinedPassiveWeight, combinedActiveWeight, minFaceQuality, passiveMinFrames and passiveWindowFrames are reported by the API but not enforced or used on the request path. onRepeatedFailure is likewise stored but not applied.
known_issues.verified: Source reading of DecisionEngineService and LivenessEngineService; grep shows no consumers for the sampling, duration and weight fields.
known_issues.recommended_fix: Implement or clearly mark each field as informational in the API.

known_issues.detail: io.mosip.liveness.engine (FaceLivenessEngine, LivenessDecisionLogic, LivenessSession) implements median-window passive voting, cold start, challenge windows, session timeouts and repeated-failure actions, and the eval harness measures PAD accuracy against labelled scenarios. Nothing in api/ or services/ references it, so none of that behaviour is reachable over HTTP.
known_issues.verified: Reference search: the engine package is referenced only by itself, io.mosip.liveness.eval and tests.
known_issues.recommended_fix: Either route the REST decision path through the engine layer, or document the HTTP path as the reduced implementation it is.

known_issues.detail: All three workflows are seeded with the same policy (0.75 / minChallengeCount 1 / 8000 ms / maxRetryCount 3 / LOCK / [blink, smile, turn_left, turn_right]), and ConfigController.getOrCreatePolicy builds the same single default for any workflow. The 'one service, three risk profiles' framing is a capability of the model rather than a configured state.
known_issues.recommended_fix: Seed distinct rows per workflow, or demonstrate the difference by applying policy updates before a demo.

known_issues.status: RESOLVED: EffectivePolicy is resolved and frozen on session creation (V4__session_policy_snapshot.sql) and persisted to policy_snapshot. Evaluated during frame and challenge processing.
known_issues.detail: Historical issue: Sessions previously re-read policy on every frame.
known_issues.resolution: Frozen policy snapshot stored on LivenessSession at creation time.

known_issues.detail: challengeTimeoutMs is copied into challenge payloads but never evaluated. ChallengeStatus.TIMEOUT is never written and there is no 'continue' action, so a client cannot distinguish 'the subject still has time' from 'that attempt failed'.
known_issues.verified: No timeout comparison exists in DecisionEngineService; grep for ChallengeStatus.TIMEOUT shows only the enum declaration and the engine layer.

known_issues.status: RESOLVED: SecurityHeadersFilter runs first (Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE) and rejects requests exceeding 24 MiB (25,165,824 bytes) with 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE.
known_issues.detail: Historical issue: No request body limit existed prior to SecurityHeadersFilter.
known_issues.resolution: Enforced by SecurityHeadersFilter with configurable mosip.security.max-request-body-bytes.

corrected_facts.source_revision: Revision 1 cited 05839c9, which is not a commit in this repository. development is at 1ed5eaa.
corrected_facts.launcher_path: Revision 1 said ./start.sh. The script is scripts/start.sh (and scripts/start.bat).
corrected_facts.passive_threshold_floor: Revision 1 said 0 is refused. 0 is accepted.
corrected_facts.challenge_timeout_floor: Revision 1 said a 15000 ms floor from mosip.liveness.min-challenge-window-ms. That property does not exist; the bound is 1000 ms.
corrected_facts.min_challenge_count_vs_pool: Revision 1 said minChallengeCount must not exceed the challenge pool. Not checked.
corrected_facts.bad_path_parameter_status: Revision 1 said 400 VALIDATION_ERROR for a bad path parameter type. Observed: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.
corrected_facts.live_path_decision: Revision 1 described median-window voting, cold start and passiveMinFrames on the live path. The live path compares a single frame's score with the threshold.
